3:## Concept
5:### Pitch
9:### Shape
11:#### Description
15:#### Checking
20:#### Downloading
25:#### Restarting

35:#### Requests
40:#### After Update
44:##### Launch
51:#### Diagnostics
### Shape

#### Description

Updates come from the edge releases, as the [EdgeReleasesScope](../edge-releases/index.md#edge-releases-scope) says, published in the GitHub repository the running build was published from, which it knows because that is baked into it. Only such a build updates itself. A build made anywhere else, as on a developer's machine, never looks for an update, never downloads one, and never replaces its binary, and the Updates section says why.

#### Checking

A check asks GitHub's releases API for the repository's releases, pre-releases included, and takes the one with the highest version `0.1.N`, comparing N as a number, never as text. It is newer only when its N is greater than the running build's; an older or equal one is never taken, so an update never goes back. A release without the asset for the running platform is passed over for the newest one that has it.
Suspense checks a few seconds after it starts, and then every 6 hours while it runs, in the background, never holding up anything else, and only while "Check for updates automatically" is on, as it is until turned off. That choice is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says. Check for updates, in the Updates section, checks straight away, whether it is on or not. A check that can't be made, as with no network or GitHub refusing it, is quiet when automatic, trying again at the next, and says why when asked for.

#### Downloading

A newer release found is downloaded straight away, in the background, taking the asset for the platform and architecture running, `suspense-0.1.N-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `suspense-0.1.N-windows-x86_64.zip`, or `suspense-0.1.N-macos-aarch64.tar.gz`. It is checked against the size GitHub gives for it, and against its SHA-256 digest where GitHub gives one, and one that doesn't match is thrown away and never used. The binary is taken out of the archive and staged beside the running binary, in the same directory, so it can be put in place by a rename, marked executable where the platform has such a mark. One download runs at a time; a newer release found while one is staged replaces it. A download that fails says so in the Updates section, and is tried again at the next check.
Where the running binary's directory can't be written, nothing is downloaded, and the Updates section says that Suspense can't update itself there, with the directory, and a link to the release's page, opened in the browser, so it can be updated by hand.

#### Restarting

Once an update is staged, a notification says "Suspense 0.1.N is ready", with a Restart button and a Later button. The Updates section says the same, with a Restart button, for as long as it stays staged. Later only closes the notification; the update stays staged, and is put in place whenever Suspense next quits.
Restart quits as quitting does, as the [MainWindowScope](../application/MainWindow.md#main-window-scope) says, asking first while work is running, and doing nothing more if the quit is cancelled, then starts Suspense again from the same path once the update is in place. However Suspense quits, a staged update is put in place as it does: the staged binary is renamed over the running one, the running one renamed aside first where the platform won't replace a running binary, as on Windows. The binary set aside is deleted at the next launch. An update left staged by a quit that never finished, as a crash, is put in place at the next launch, before anything else, and takes effect at the launch after, the Updates section saying a restart finishes it.
Putting an update in place never leaves Suspense without a binary: a step that fails puts back the binary that was there, and the Updates section says why it couldn't update.

#### Updates Section

The [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope) has an "Updates" section. It says the running version, as "Suspense 0.1.42", and where it can't update itself, as for a build made elsewhere, why, and offers nothing else. Otherwise it shows a checkbox reading "Check for updates automatically", a "Check for updates" button, disabled while a check or download is under way, and a line saying where things stand: "Checking for updates…", "Suspense is up to date", checked when, as "Checked 5 minutes ago", "Downloading 0.1.N…" with how much has come, "Suspense 0.1.N is ready" with a Restart button, or, in the theme's error colour, why the last check, download, or update failed.

#### Requests

Every request to GitHub sends a User-Agent naming Suspense and its version, as "Suspense/0.1.42", since GitHub refuses requests without one, and asks for its JSON with `Accept: application/vnd.github+json`. A check asks for the repository's releases at `https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<name>/releases`, 100 to a page, so the newest edge release is never missed for being past the first page, and takes the highest N among the releases whose tag is `v0.1.N`, ignoring drafts and any release whose tag isn't of that form. An asset is downloaded from its `browser_download_url`, following GitHub's redirects to where it is stored, and its digest, given as `sha256:<hex>`, is compared without regard to case.
GitHub's limit on requests made without signing in is respected: a check refused for it, with a 403 or 429 and its rate-limit headers, says so, "GitHub's rate limit was reached; try again after" and the time it resets, and an automatic check isn't tried again before then. Any other refusal says the status GitHub gave and its message, never only that the check failed.

#### After Update

An update that has been put in place is confirmed at the next

##### Launch

the version now running is compared with the one staged, and

where they match, a notification says "Updated to Suspense 0.1.N", and the Updates section says so until the next check. Where they don't, as when the binary put in place still reports the old version, the Updates section says, in the theme's error colour, that the update to 0.1.N didn't take effect, and the same release is never downloaded and put in place again by itself, so an update can never loop, one restart after another; a Check for updates asked for by hand still tries it.
The binary set aside is deleted at the next launch, and where it can't be yet, as on Windows while the process that ran it is still exiting, it is tried again at each launch after, never stopping the launch. A staged binary left beside the running one that is no newer than it is deleted rather than put in place.

#### Diagnostics

Suspense keeps a log of what updating does, `updates.log` in its own data directory, beside its preferences, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) keeps them: one line per step, with the time, each check with the repository and running version it checked for, the releases it found and the one it took or why it took none, each download with its asset, size, and digest check, each staging, each putting in place with its paths and how it went, and each launch's confirmation, every failure with its whole error. It keeps the last 1,000 lines.
The Updates section has a "Details" disclosure, collapsed to start with, that shows what updating rests on: the running version, the repository it updates from, or that it has none and so is not an edge build, the running binary's path and whether its directory can be written, the last check's time and the newest release it found, and what is staged, if anything, with a "Show log" button that opens `updates.log` as the [OpenFileScope](../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) opens a file, and a "Copy" button that puts all of it, with the log's last 50 lines, on the clipboard, for a bug report.

content.text:
I couldn't find a single definite bug in the self-update code. The mechanics look right: the version and repository are baked into edge builds, downloads follow GitHub's redirects, the binary is swapped on quit (including Windows' rename-aside), and Restart relaunches. What I did find is that it could fail without leaving any trace, plus two real gaps. All 526 tests pass; I haven't run a real update against GitHub.

**What could have gone wrong unseen:**
- **Errors were thrown away.** Requests used `curl -f`, so GitHub's status and message never came through. An automatic check that failed said nothing at all, and one you asked for said only "couldn't reach GitHub". GitHub's rate limit for requests that aren't signed in (60 an hour per network address) would have looked like "nothing happens".
- **No version check when applying.** Any staged binary was put in place at quit or launch, even one no newer than the running version.
- **No protection against a loop.** If an update put in place still reported the old version, it would be downloaded and applied again on every check.
- **The User-Agent sent no version** (`suspense`). GitHub accepts that, but the spec asks for `Suspense/0.1.N`.

**What I changed** (`src/self_update.rs`, `src/settings_window.rs`, `src/main.rs`, `src/version.rs`):
- **Requests:**
  - They send `User-Agent: Suspense/0.1.N`.
  - Only non-draft `v0.1.N` tags count.
  - The digest is compared ignoring case.
- **Refusals:**
  - A rate limit says "GitHub's rate limit was reached; try again after 2026-10-05 11:33 UTC", and automatic checks wait until then.
  - Any other refusal says GitHub's status and message, e.g. "GitHub refused the check (404): Not Found".
- **After an update:**
  - Putting an update in place records its version. The next launch compares it with the version running and shows "Updated to Suspense 0.1.N".
  - If they don't match, the Updates section reports it in red, and that release isn't applied again automatically. Check for updates still tries it.
  - A staged binary that isn't newer is deleted. The set-aside binary is retried at each launch.
- **Log:** `updates.log` (last 1,000 lines) sits beside the preferences in Suspense's config folder. It records every check, the releases found and the one taken or why none, each download with its size and digest check, staging, putting in place with paths, and each launch's confirmation, with full errors.
- **Details:** a collapsed "Details" section under Settings → Updates shows the version, the repository (or that this isn't an edge build), the binary's path and whether its folder can be written, the last check and newest release found, and what's staged. "Show log" opens `updates.log` in the editor, and "Copy" copies everything plus the log's last 50 lines.
- **`--version`:** it now prints `Suspense 0.1.42 (owner/name)` or `Suspense 0.1.0 (development build)`.
- **Release check (`.github/workflows/edge.yml`):** each platform's job now runs the built binary with `--version` and fails if it doesn't report the version and repository it was given. This hasn't run in CI yet.

**What to check:** once you're running an edge build with this change, open Settings → Updates → Details and press "Copy", or look in `updates.log`. That will show which step fails on your machine.

The spec and the prompt agree.
